bibl.title: The Neurophysiology of Memory
bibl.publisher: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: These cross-species comparisons show that the patterns of mnemonic activity observed throughout the medial temporal lobe are largely conserved across species.

span.label: medial temporal lobe neuronal correlates of recognition and associative memory
span.quote: To address this question, we examine the neurophysiological correlates of both recognition and associative memory in the medial temporal lobe of humans, monkeys, and rats.

span.label: review
span.quote: In this chapter, we review the neurophysiological findings that address these two main points.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because the hippocampus receives polymodal rather than unimodal input, it is positioned to combine the cortex's stimulus-selective signals into complex conjunctions or to abstract a general output signal from them, which is why its mnemonic code is abstracted rather than stimulus-specific
span.quote: The hippocampus is in a privileged position to either combine the stimulus-selective mnemonic information in cortex into more complex conjunctions or to abstract, from the stimulus-selective information, a more general “output” signal.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The occasional stimulus-selective, cortex-type recognition signals seen in the hippocampus are inherited through the direct anatomical projections from perirhinal and entorhinal cortex to area CA1
span.quote: These “cortexlike” recognition signals may be conveyed via the direct projections from both the perirhinal and the entorhinal cortices to area CA1.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: At long delays interference builds up, so contextual/episodic conjunctive information becomes the useful cue for recognition, which is why hippocampal damage bites hardest at long delays
span.quote: At longer delay intervals, when interference can play a detrimental role, information about the context or episode in which the stimulus was seen could be particularly helpful to successful performance.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Cortical stimulus-stimulus association works by a cue acquiring the capacity to generate the neural representation of the stimulus it was paired with, producing pair-coding and pair-recall firing
span.quote: Thus, within these cortical areas, stimulus-stimulus associations may be represented by the acquired capacity of a stimulus to generate the neural representation of another stimulus with which it has been associated.

span.label: The parahippocampal/postrhinal cortex is excluded from the review because too little is known about its mnemonic activity.
span.quote: Much less is known about the patterns of mnemonic activity in the parahippocampal/postrhinal cortex, and therefore this region will not be discussed.

span.label: No direct comparison exists that would identify which testing conditions produce similar versus different coding in cortex and hippocampus.
span.quote: A compelling direct comparison that reveals the critical aspects of these different testing conditions has yet to be made.

span.label: The scope of associative-memory signals across the medial temporal lobe is not yet established.
span.quote: Additional comparative studies are needed to determine the full scope of neural signals underlying associative memory across the medial temporal lobe.

span.label: A specific empirical gap: intervening stimuli have not been tested against selective delay activity in rat perirhinal/entorhinal cortex.
span.quote: The effect of intervening stimuli on the selective delay activity in the perirhinal or entorhinal cortices of rats has not been examined.

span.label: The anatomy is used to support two opposite expectations, both stated in the same passage.
span.quote: On the one hand, the fact that each of these structures differs markedly in the amount and content of convergent cortical input suggests that each area may be able to process or combine information to encode, store, or retrieve memory in different ways. This view suggests that each area may be characterized by distinct patterns of mnemonic activity

span.label: How many neurons show the effect depends on which version of the task was run.
span.quote: However, the proportion of neurons exhibiting match enhancement was substantially higher during performance of the ABBA version of the task compared to the standard version

span.label: The neuropsychological literature is stated to give only indirect insight into neural activity.
span.quote: neuropsychological studies on braindamaged patients or experimental animals can provide only indirect insights into the specific patterns of neural activity that allow us to form and retain new long-term declarative memories

span.label: match enhancement
span.quote: However, the proportion of neurons exhibiting match enhancement was substantially higher during performance of the ABBA version of the task compared to the standard version

span.label: ABBA version
span.quote: However, the proportion of neurons exhibiting match enhancement was substantially higher during performance of the ABBA version of the task compared to the standard version

span.label: convergent cortical input
span.quote: On the one hand, the fact that each of these structures differs markedly in the amount and content of convergent cortical input suggests that each area may be able to process or combine information to encode, store, or retrieve memory in different ways. This view suggests that each area may be characterized by distinct patterns of mnemonic activity

span.label: parallel projections
span.quote: On the other hand, the strong parallel projections from the perirhinal and parahippocampal/ postrhinal cortices to both the entorhinal cortex and area CA1 suggest that neurons in all of these regions have access to similar kinds of sensory/mnemonic information

span.label: declarative memories
span.quote: neuropsychological studies on braindamaged patients or experimental animals can provide only indirect insights into the specific patterns of neural activity that allow us to form and retain new long-term declarative memories

span.label: the anatomical argument - TWO OPPOSITE PREDICTIONS FROM THE SAME STRUCTURES: differing convergent cortical input is read as predicting distinct mnemonic patterns per area, and strong parallel projections as predicting shared access to similar information; both are stated, so neither a difference nor a similarity result can discriminate between them
span.quote: On the one hand, the fact that each of these structures differs markedly in the amount and content of convergent cortical input suggests that each area may be able to process or combine information to encode, store, or retrieve memory in different ways. This view suggests that each area may be characterized by distinct patterns of mnemonic activity

span.label: match enhancement - A PROPORTION THAT MOVES WITH THE PROTOCOL: substantially more neurons show it in the ABBA version of the task than in the standard version, so 'how many neurons do X' is a fact about the task that was run as much as about the tissue
span.quote: However, the proportion of neurons exhibiting match enhancement was substantially higher during performance of the ABBA version of the task compared to the standard version

span.label: neuropsychological evidence - INDIRECT BY THE AUTHORS' OWN DESCRIPTION: lesion work on patients and animals is said to provide only indirect insight into the specific patterns of neural activity, which is why the review turns to recording
span.quote: neuropsychological studies on braindamaged patients or experimental animals can provide only indirect insights into the specific patterns of neural activity that allow us to form and retain new long-term declarative memories

span.label: builds-on → Sakai and Miyashita (ref. 52), pair-coding neurons; and Wood et al. (ref. 37), conjunctive coding neurons
span.quote: Yet the evidence showing differences between these areas suggests that parahippocampal cortical neurons may participate in associative memory by developing representations of complex perceptual stimuli that can be activated by their associates (i.e., pair-coding neurons of Sakai and Miyashita52), whereas neurons of the hippocampal formation participate in associative memory by representing conjunctions of independent perceptual stimuli as well as behavioral events (i.e., conjunctive coding neurons of Wood et al.37).

span.label: ABBA version —causes→ match enhancement
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: However, the proportion of neurons exhibiting match enhancement was substantially higher during performance of the ABBA version of the task compared to the standard version

span.label: Across humans, monkeys and rats the patterns of memory-related firing in the medial temporal lobe are largely the same, so mnemonic signals are conserved across species.
span.quote: These cross-species comparisons show that the patterns of mnemonic activity observed throughout the medial temporal lobe are largely conserved across species.

span.label: Perirhinal and entorhinal neurons signal recognition with stimulus-selective suppressed or enhanced responses to a repeated item, whereas hippocampal neurons signal an abstracted match/nonmatch outcome that generalises over all stimuli.
span.quote: In contrast to the stimulus-selective recognition signals observed in cortex, neurons of the hippocampal formation convey abstracted recognition memory signals.

span.label: Entorhinal selective delay activity survives multiple intervening test stimuli while perirhinal delay activity is abolished by even one intervening stimulus, dissociating the two cortical areas.
span.quote: By contrast, selective delay activity in the perirhinal cortex was disrupted by the presentation of even a single intervening stimulus.

span.label: Match-suppression neurons suppress to any stimulus repetition including behaviourally irrelevant repeats, whereas match-enhancement neurons respond only when the behaviourally relevant (target) stimulus repeats.
span.quote: By contrast, the match-enhancement neurons were enhanced only when the behaviorally relevant stimulus was repeated.

span.label: Match suppression is not sensory fatigue or habituation, because the suppression is abolished when the same stimulus reappears as the sample on the next trial.
span.quote: The match-suppression response cannot be explained by sensory fatigue or habituation, because the suppression disappears when the same stimulus is shown as a sample on the following trial.

span.label: Entorhinal place cells keep the same spatial firing pattern when a rat is moved between a circular and a square environment, while hippocampal place cells almost always remap to independent patterns.
span.quote: By contrast, hippocampal neurons nearly always showed different and independent patterns of spatial activity in the two environments.

span.label: Lesion evidence dissociates the two regions by delay: entorhinal/perirhinal damage impairs recognition even at short delays, whereas hippocampus-limited damage impairs recognition most strongly at delays of many minutes to hours.
span.quote: In contrast to lesion studies involving the cortical medial temporal lobe areas, damage limited to the hippocampus produces the most striking recognition impairments when delay intervals are long (many minutes to hours)

span.label: About a third to two fifths of human hippocampal and entorhinal neurons recorded at retrieval are modulated by whether the item is new or old, mostly by enhancing their response to previously seen stimuli.
span.quote: The responses of 35% (10 of 29) of cells recorded in the human hippocampus and 40% (8 of 20) of cells recorded in the entorhinal cortex in the retrieval phase were influenced by whether a stimulus was new or old.

span.label: Cortical and hippocampal areas contribute different forms of associative coding: perirhinal/inferotemporal pair-coding and pair-recall neurons link one stimulus to its learned associate, while hippocampal neurons code conjunctions of stimulus with place and behavioural event.
span.quote: “Pair-recall” neurons increased their firing rate during the delay period following presentation of the associate of the optimal cue, leading up to a robust response to that cue.

span.label: associative memory
span.quote: We define associative memory in a broad sense to include any memory about the relationship between two or more items.

span.label: priming
span.quote: Priming is defined as an improvement in the ability to detect or identify stimuli as the result of previous experience with the stimuli.

span.label: hippocampal formation
span.quote: These structures include the hippocampal formation (defined here as the dentate gyrus, areas CA3, CA1, and the subiculum) and the entorhinal, perirhinal, and parahippocampal cortices.

span.label: "abstracted" recognition signal
span.quote: This pattern of activity has been referred to as an “abstracted” recognition signal in the sense that these hippocampal neurons do not convey specific information about particular stimuli but, instead, appear to signal the outcome of the match-nonmatch comparison (i.e., the answer) for all stimuli.

span.label: conjunctive coding
span.quote: The pattern of activity exhibited by the second subset of neurons has been referred to as “conjunctive coding” and can be considered a form of associative memory

span.label: match-suppression / match-enhancement signals
span.quote: These so-called match-suppression or match-enhancement signals convey information about the previous occurrence of a particular stimulus on a given trial.

span.label: familiarity effect
span.quote: This pattern of activity (referred to as the familiarity effect) is seen as animals passively view repeated stimuli

span.label: match versus nonmatch status of the test stimulus
span.term: match versus nonmatch status of the test stimulus
span.quote: The only difference between the two stimulus presentations was that in the match condition (and not in the nonmatch condition), the animals carried a memory of having seen the stimulus at the beginning of the trial.

span.label: physical characteristics of the test stimulus
span.term: physical characteristics of the test stimulus
span.quote: Importantly, the physical characteristics of the stimulus were identical in both the “match” and the “nonmatch” conditions.

span.label: neuronal response magnitude to the preferred stimulus (suppressed or enhanced)
span.term: neuronal response magnitude to the preferred stimulus (suppressed or enhanced)
span.quote: This analysis showed that neurons in the entorhinal and perirhinal cortices signaled the occurrence of a matching stimulus with either a suppressed (decreased) or an enhanced (increased) response.

span.label: spatial location of odor presentation
span.quote: The location of the odor presentation changed on each trial but did not predict whether the trial was a nonmatch or a match.

span.label: length of the delay interval and number of intervening test stimuli
span.term: length of the delay interval and number of intervening test stimuli
span.quote: Other variations of the task include the use of either highly familiar or novel stimuli, the use of varying numbers of “test” stimuli presented between the sample stimulus and the final match, or variations in the length of the delay intervals used.

span.label: 47% ... 94% — proportion of visually responsive monkey entorhinal (47%) versus perirhinal (94%) neurons that respond selectively to particular visual stimuli
span.quote: For example, in monkeys, 47% of the visually responsive neurons in the entorhinal cortex18 and 94% of the visually responsive neurons in the perirhinal cortex19 respond selectively to particular visual stimuli.

span.label: 35% ... 11% — proportion of sampled rat lateral entorhinal (35%) versus perirhinal (11%) neurons with odor-specific firing
span.quote: In rats, 35% of the sampled lateral entorhinal neurons and 11% of the sampled perirhinal neurons exhibit odor-specific firing properties.

span.label: 15 of 120 or 12.5% — share of responsive hippocampal neurons that differentiated match from nonmatch presentations
span.quote: some neurons in this region respond differentially to stimuli when they are shown as matches compared to when the same stimuli are shown as nonmatches (15 of 120 or 12.5% of the responsive neurons)

span.label: 13 of 91 or 14% — share of responsive rat hippocampal neurons carrying an abstracted match-nonmatch signal independent of odor identity
span.quote: some neurons signaled the match-nonmatch status of an odor irrespective of the odor identity (“abstracted” match-nonmatch signal; 13 of 91 or 14% of the responsive neurons)

span.label: 18 of 91 or 20% ... 4 of 91 or 4% — share of responsive hippocampal neurons coding match-nonmatch status conjointly with position (20%), or with both position and odor identity (4%)
span.quote: A second subset of neurons in this task signaled the abstracted match-nonmatch signals in conjunction either with the position in which it occurred (18 of 91 or 20% of the responsive neurons) or with both position as well as odor identity (4 of 91 or 4%)

span.label: 24 hours — longest delay across which repetition suppression to a once-novel stimulus persists
span.quote: For some neurons, the firing rate is suppressed when the novel stimulus is repeated, even after a delay interval of 24 hours.

span.label: 74 neurons in 3 regions — size of the human single-unit sample in the recognition study whose results matched the animal cortical pattern
span.quote: Despite the relatively small number of neurons examined (74 neurons in 3 regions), the overall pattern of activity was strikingly similar to the findings described for the perirhinal and entorhinal neurons in rats and monkeys.

span.label: 24 — number of fractal stimulus patterns used in the paired-associate study of inferotemporal and perirhinal neurons
span.quote: examined responses of anterior inferotemporal and perirhinal neurons to 24 fractal stimulus patterns

span.label: between 1 and 10 hours — encoding-to-retrieval interval in the human single-unit recognition task, a delay known to challenge amnesic patients
span.quote: the retrieval phase in this task occurred between 1 and 10 hours after the encoding phase
